data.name: get_patterns
data.text:
## tabs — Tabs (component, archetype navigate)
A set of peer views sharing one space, one visible at a time, switched by labelled controls.
Aliases: tab bar, segmented control, tab strip
Anatomy: Tab (One label); Panel (The view it shows); Indicator (Which is current)
Related — uses: badge, menu | neighbors: view-switcher, accordion, carousel
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Placement and overflow [layout] — Where are tabs, and what happens when there are too many?
  - placement (single-select: one id) — Placement
      top: Top (e.g. Browser tabs)
      bottom: Bottom (e.g. iOS tab bars)
      vertical: Vertical (e.g. Edge vertical tabs)
      segmented-control: Segmented control (e.g. iOS segmented controls)
  - overflow (single-select: one id) — Overflow
      scroll: Scroll (e.g. Material scrollable tabs)
      shrink: Shrink (e.g. Chrome tabs)
      more-menu: More menu (e.g. Office ribbons)
      wrap: Wrap (e.g. Old desktop dialogs)
* Labels [content] — What does a tab say?
  - label (multi-select: list of ids) — Label content
      text: Text (e.g. GitHub repository tabs)
      icon: Icon (e.g. Bottom tab bars)
      badge-count: Badge count (e.g. Unread counts)
      favicon-and-title: Favicon and title (e.g. Browser tabs)
      close-button: Close button (e.g. Editor tabs)
* Tab origin and grouping [composition] — Who makes tabs, and can they be grouped?
  - origin (single-select: one id) — Origin
      fixed-by-the-designer: Fixed by the designer (e.g. Settings tabs)
      created-by-the-person: Created by the person (e.g. Browser tabs; CHI '25 probe overviews)
      saved-views: Saved views (e.g. Notion database views)
      pinned-and-preview-tabs: Pinned and preview tabs — A preview tab is replaced unless kept (e.g. VS Code preview tabs)
  - grouping (single-select: one id) — Grouping
      flat: Flat (e.g. Most tab sets)
      tab-groups: Tab groups (e.g. Chrome tab groups)
      nested-tabs: Nested tabs (e.g. Tabs inside a tab panel)
* Background tabs [lifecycle] — What happens to a tab you are not looking at?
  - background (single-select: one id) — Background state
      unloaded-on-switch: Unloaded on switch (e.g. Simple tab widgets)
      kept-alive: Kept alive (e.g. Editor tabs)
      put-to-sleep: Put to sleep (e.g. Edge sleeping tabs)
* Switching [invocation] — How does a person switch?
  - switchBy (multi-select: list of ids) — Switch by
      click: Click (e.g. All)
      swipe-between-panels: Swipe between panels (e.g. Android tab layouts)
      keyboard: Keyboard (e.g. Ctrl+Tab)
      search-tabs: Search tabs (e.g. Chrome tab search)

## card — Card (component, archetype browse-collections)
A bounded container that summarizes one item; the most common item view inside overviews.
Aliases: tile, item card
Anatomy: Media (Image or video); Header (Title and subtitle); Body (Key attributes); Actions (What can be done to the item)
Related — uses: badge, menu | neighbors: stat-tile
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Card content [content] — What goes on the card?
  - media (single-select: one id) — Media
      none: None (e.g. Linear issue cards)
      top-image: Top image (e.g. Airbnb listings)
      side-thumbnail: Side thumbnail (e.g. Spotify search results)
      full-bleed-background: Full-bleed background (e.g. App Store Today cards)
  - actions (single-select: one id) — Actions
      none: None — The card only opens (e.g. News cards)
      one-primary-action: One primary action (e.g. Add to cart on a product card)
      action-row: Action row (e.g. Social post actions)
      overflow-menu: Overflow menu (e.g. Google Drive file cards)
* Form [layout] — What shape and weight does the card take?
  - shape (single-select: one id) — Shape
      vertical: Vertical (e.g. Product grids)
      horizontal: Horizontal (e.g. Search result rows)
      compact-tile: Compact tile (e.g. Home screen widgets)
  - style (single-select: one id) — Container styl

data.name: get_patterns
data.text:
## modal-dialog — Modal dialog (component, archetype navigate)
A window over the page that holds interaction until it is dismissed, used for focused tasks, confirmations and quick detail.
Aliases: modal, dialog, pop-up, lightbox
Anatomy: Backdrop (What dims the page); Container (The dialog surface); Actions (How it ends)
Related — neighbors: drawer, popover, bottom-sheet
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Size and position [layout] — How big is it, and where?
  - form (single-select: one id) — Form
      centered-small: Centered small (e.g. Alert dialogs)
      centered-large: Centered large (e.g. Airtable expanded record)
      full-screen: Full screen (e.g. Material full-screen dialog on mobile)
      sheet-from-an-edge: Sheet from an edge (e.g. iOS sheets)
      lightbox: Lightbox — Media on a dark backdrop (e.g. Photo viewers)
      anchored-bubble: Anchored bubble — The dialog opens attached to the element that raised it — a time slot, a cell — rather than centred, at an edge or full screen, while still holding interaction until it is answered (e.g. Google Calendar — Event creation box)
* Opening and closing [invocation] — What opens it, and what closes it?
  - openBy (multi-select: list of ids) — Opened by
      user-action: User action (e.g. Quick view buttons)
      system-initiated: System-initiated (e.g. Session timeout warnings)
      url: URL — The dialog has its own address (e.g. Instagram web posts)
      keyboard-shortcut: Keyboard shortcut (e.g. Slack Cmd+K)
  - dismissBy (multi-select: list of ids) — Dismissed by
      close-button: Close button (e.g. Most dialogs)
      escape: Escape (e.g. Most desktop dialogs)
      click-the-backdrop: Click the backdrop (e.g. Lightboxes)
      swipe-down: Swipe down (e.g. iOS sheets)
      only-by-completing: Only by completing (e.g. Required consent dialogs)
* Modality [scope] — What does it block?
  - modality (single-select: one id) — Modality
      blocking: Blocking (e.g. Alerts)
      modeless: Modeless — The page stays usable (e.g. Word Find and Replace)
      stacked: Stacked — Dialogs over dialogs (e.g. Settings sub-dialogs)
* Contents [content] — What is it for?
  - purpose (single-select: one id) — Purpose
      confirmation: Confirmation (e.g. Delete dialogs)
      form: Form (e.g. Create issue)
      detail-view: Detail view (e.g. Retail quick view)
      media: Media (e.g. Lightbox)
      multi-step-task: Multi-step task (e.g. Setup wizards)
      selection-list: Selection list — A list to choose one option from (which playlist to add to, where to share) — not a confirmation, a filled-in form, a detail view, media, or a multi-step task. (e.g. Apple Music — Add to a Playlist sheet)
* Unsaved work [feedback] — What happens to work when it closes?
  - onDismiss (single-select: one id) — On dismiss
      discard-silently: Discard silently (e.g. Simple forms)
      confirm-before-discarding: Confirm before discarding (e.g. GitHub new issue)
      keep-a-draft: Keep a draft (e.g. Slack message drafts)
      already-saved: Already saved — Edits made inside the dialog persist as they are made, so closing discards nothing (Airtable expanded record) (e.g. Airtable — Expanded record)

## media-player — Media player (pattern, archetype consume-media)
A stage and transport for playing video or audio, with position, quality and optional overlays under the person’s control.
Aliases: video player, audio player, playback controls
Anatomy: Stage (Where the media renders); Transport bar (Play, seek, volume); Chrome (Title, creator and actions); Overlays (Captions, chapters, ads)
Related — uses: slider, menu, toast, progress-indicator | specializes: consume-media | neighbors: playlist-queue, timeline-editor
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Transport controls [flow] — Which playback controls are available?
  - controls (multi-select: list of ids) — Controls
      play-pause: Play pause (e.g. YouTube)
      scrubber: Scru

data.text:
## badge — Badge (component, archetype monitor)
A small indicator on another element showing a count or a status.
Aliases: counter, notification dot, status pill
Anatomy: Host (What it is attached to); Indicator (Count, dot or label)
Related — neighbors: stat-tile, progress-indicator
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Meaning [content] — What does the badge say?
  - meaning (single-select: one id) — Meaning
      count: Count (e.g. Unread messages)
      dot: Dot — Something new (e.g. App icon dots)
      status: Status (e.g. Online presence)
      label: Label (e.g. New or Beta)
* Overflow [encoding] — How are large counts shown?
  - overflow (single-select: one id) — Overflow
      exact-count: Exact count (e.g. Mail folders)
      capped: Capped — 99+ (e.g. Many apps)
      dot-past-a-threshold: Dot past a threshold (e.g. Minimal badges)
* What counts [initiative] — Who decides what increments it?
  - rule (single-select: one id) — Counting rule
      everything-unread: Everything unread (e.g. Default mail badges)
      only-mentions: Only mentions (e.g. Slack mentions-only badge setting)
      the-person-s-rule: The person’s rule (e.g. Custom inbox counts)
      pending-actions: Pending actions — The badge counts work waiting for the person — updates to install, apps to update, tasks to finish — rather than anything read, unread or addressed to them; the counting rules as written assume a message inbox (e.g. iOS Settings — App icon)
* Aggregation [scope] — Does it roll up?
  - aggregation (single-select: one id) — Aggregation
      per-item: Per item (e.g. Folder counts)
      rolled-up-to-parent: Rolled up to parent (e.g. Account totals)
      app-icon-total: App icon total (e.g. iOS app badges)
      device-total: Device total — One indicator for every unread notification on the device, on system chrome rather than on any app's icon or nav entry (watch faces, always-on displays) (e.g. Apple Watch — Watch face)
